title: Beyond the 956: Sir Patrick Stewart, Star Trek's Captain Picard and X-Men's Professor X, dies at 86

content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Sir Patrick Stewart, the celebrated actor who commanded the USS Enterprise as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek and led the X-Men as Professor Charles Xavier on the big screen, has died at 86.

Stewart died on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, at his home in Los Angeles. His family announced his death the next day, saying he died in the loving care of his wife, Sunny Ozell, “following a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s Disease and Lewy Body Dementia,” according to a statement shared by his representative, Kelly Bush Novak.

His official cause of death was confirmed on November 19, when his death certificate, obtained by TMZ from the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner, listed cardiopulmonary arrest and a neurocognitive disorder with Lewy body. The certificate also noted that his remains were handled on November 3 through alkaline hydrolysis, commonly known as water cremation.

Born July 13, 1940, in Mirfield, Yorkshire, England, Stewart built his career on the stage with the Royal Shakespeare Company before becoming one of the most recognizable faces in science fiction. He played Captain Picard in Star Trek: The Next Generation from 1987 to 1994 and in four Star Trek films, then brought Professor X to life in the X-Men film series, a role he was set to reprise in Avengers: Doomsday. He was knighted by Queen Elizabeth II in 2010 for his services to drama.

Stewart is survived by his wife, Sunny Ozell.

Sources: USA Today; Entertainment Weekly; Page Six; TMZ via CBR.
